mainTopic: רבא's rulings on borrowed walls, sunlight through the walls (רבי יאשיה), אביי's list of תנאים who require a דירת קבע, and רבי יוחנן's round סוכה.
overview: The amud opens with two rulings of רבא. סכך over a מבוי with a לחי is a כשרה סוכה, and so is סכך over פסי ביראות. The גמרא explains why each ruling is needed (צריכותא), including a third ruling that goes from the laws of סוכה to the laws of שבת. Next the משנה says a סוכה with more sun than shade is פסולה. A ברייתא records a מחלוקת: the תנא קמא counts only sunlight through the סכך, while רבי יאשיה also counts sunlight through the walls, based on the פסוק about the פרוכת. אביי then lists eight תנאים who all hold that a סוכה must be a דירת קבע, and the גמרא shows the source for each one. Finally, רבי יוחנן rules that a round סוכה needs room for twenty-four people around its edge, following רבי's four-by-four-אמות minimum. The גמרא challenges this with math showing that twelve should be enough. The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Roofing over an alleyway with a side post is kosher
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that סכך placed over a מבוי that has a לחי makes a כשרה סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone put סכך over an alleyway that has a side post, it is a kosher סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא (named on the previous amud) gives a ruling: a מבוי with a לחי can serve as a סוכה if you put סכך on top.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מבוי gives you two real side walls. The לחי is only a thin post, but for שבת it counts as closing off the alley. רבא says it also counts as a wall-element for סוכה, so the structure is כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: A side post at the alley's entrance that legally 'closes' it

phrases.english: If one placed roofing over an alleyway
phrases.notes: The two side walls of the alley serve as walls of the סוכה.

phrases.english: that has a side post — it is kosher.
phrases.notes: The לחי counts toward the walls needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: סִיכֵּךְ עַל גַּבֵּי מָבוֹי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ לֶחִי כְּשֵׁרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's statement, which was introduced on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סכך over a מבוי with a לחי is a כשרה סוכה, because the לחי counts as a wall-element.

steps.title: Roofing over the corner posts around a well is kosher
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a second ruling: סכך placed over פסי ביראות makes a כשרה סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: if someone put סכך over the posts around a well, it is a kosher סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second, parallel ruling. Here the 'walls' are only the corner posts set up around a well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסי ביראות are four L-shaped corner pieces around a well. Between them there are big open gaps. For שבת, חז"ל let them count as a full enclosure as a leniency for festival pilgrims. רבא says that this also works for סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Corner boards set up around a well that legally enclose it for שבת
An אמורא who gives these rulings

steps.confusionAlert: Most of the area around the well is actually open. The posts are only at the corners, yet the הלכה still treats them as walls.

phrases.english: And Rava said: if one placed roofing over
the boards surrounding wells — it is kosher.
phrases.notes: The four corner posts count as walls.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא סִיכֵּךְ עַל גַּבֵּי פַּסֵּי בֵירָאוֹת כְּשֵׁרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling by רבא with a similar theme. It sets up the question of why both rulings are needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סכך over פסי ביראות is a כשרה סוכה.

steps.title: Why the alleyway case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins explaining why both rulings are necessary. From the מבוי alone, we might think its two real walls are what make it work, and that would not carry over to the well posts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both rulings are needed. If רבא had only taught the alleyway, we would say it works because it has two real, full walls. But the posts around wells do not have two full walls, so we would say they don't work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: why did רבא need to say two similar rulings? It shows that the first ruling alone would not teach the second.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מבוי has a special strength: two full, solid walls. A learner could think that strength is the reason it is כשרה. פסי ביראות have no full walls at all, only corners, so we would wrongly disqualify them.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is necessary (to state both cases)
I would say no (it is not valid)

phrases.english: And it is necessary.
phrases.notes: This opens a צריכותא: both rulings are needed.

phrases.english: For if he had taught us only the alleyway,
that is because there are two full-fledged walls.
phrases.notes: The two side walls of the alley.

phrases.english: But regarding the boards surrounding wells,

phrases.aramaic: דְּלֵיכָּא שְׁתֵּי דְפָנוֹת מְעַלְּיָיתָא — אֵימָא לָא.
phrases.english: where there are not two full-fledged walls — I would say no.
phrases.notes: There are only corner pieces with open gaps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the two rulings in steps 1 and 2 are not redundant.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case has a unique strength, so neither can be learned from the other.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If only the מבוי were taught, we would think its validity depends on having two full walls, and we would disqualify פסי ביראות.
steps.terutzMaskana: So רבא had to say the פסי ביראות case explicitly.

steps.title: Why the well-posts case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the צריכותא. From the well posts alone, we might think having the 'name' of four walls is what makes it work, and the alleyway lacks that.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if רבא had only taught the posts around wells, we would say it works because it has the 'name' of four walls. But an alleyway does not have the name of four walls, so we would say it doesn't work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the other side. The second ruling alone would not teach the first, so רבא needed both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסי ביראות have a corner piece on all four sides, so they carry the 'name' of four walls. A מבוי does not have that. It has only two real walls plus a לחי. Each case has a different strength, so each had to be stated on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'name' or category of four walls

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's two rulings complement each other. The מבוי has full walls but not four of them. The פסי ביראות have four 'walls' but none of them is full. Each could have been dismissed on its own, so both were needed.

phrases.english: And if he had taught us only the boards surrounding wells,
that is because it has the name of four walls,
phrases.notes: There is a corner piece on each of the four sides.

phrases.english: but if one placed roofing over an alleyway,

phrases.aramaic: דְּלֵיכָּא שֵׁם אַרְבַּע דְפָנוֹת — אֵימָא לָא.
phrases.english: where there is not the name of four walls — I would say no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided צריכותא begun in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: the reverse side of the explanation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If only the פסי ביראות were taught, we would think validity depends on having the 'name' of four walls, and we would disqualify the מבוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both rulings are necessary. Neither case can be learned from the other.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא's two statements are both needed, since each case's validity could be tied to a feature the other lacks.

steps.title: Why the third ruling is also needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the צריכותא. With only the first two rulings, we would know that walls can be borrowed from שבת for סוכה, but not that walls can be borrowed from סוכה for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if רבא had taught us only these two rulings (מבוי and פסי ביראות), we would say that you can learn from the strict laws (שבת) to the lenient laws (סוכה). But from the lenient laws to the strict laws, I would say no. So the third ruling is necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבא also needed his third ruling: a סוכה made properly with two walls plus a טפח counts as walls for שבת too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first two rulings, something that works as a wall for שבת (the stricter area) is used for סוכה (the more lenient area). That direction is easy to accept. The third ruling goes the other way: a wall that is only good enough for סוכה is used for שבת. Without this ruling, we would not have known that.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught us; he told us
The stricter area of law (here, the laws of שבת)
The more lenient area of law (here, the laws of סוכה)
It is necessary; each ruling teaches something new

steps.whatToRemember: All three of רבא's rulings are needed. מבוי teaches about two real walls. פסי ביראות teaches about the 'name' of four walls. The סוכה ruling teaches that walls can carry over from the lenient area (סוכה) to the strict area (שבת).
steps.confusionAlert: The two directions sound alike, but they are not. 'From the strict to the lenient' means using a שבת wall for a סוכה. 'From the lenient to the strict' means using a סוכה wall for שבת. The third ruling is about the second direction.

phrases.english: And if he had taught us only these two
phrases.notes: The rulings about the מבוי and the פסי ביראות.

phrases.english: [we would say these work because they go] from the strict to the lenient
phrases.notes: From שבת walls to סוכה.

phrases.english: but from the lenient to the strict
phrases.notes: From סוכה walls to שבת.

phrases.english: I would say no; [so the third ruling] is necessary

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכותא begun in steps 3 and 4 by justifying רבא's third ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: shows that each ruling teaches something the others cannot
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only the first two rulings, walls could carry over only from strict (שבת) to lenient (סוכה), not the other way.
steps.terutzMaskana: The third ruling shows that a valid סוכה wall (two walls plus a טפח) also counts as a wall for שבת.

steps.title: The משנה: more sun than shade is invalid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes its next rule: a סוכה with more sunlight than shade is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a סוכה whose sunlight is more than its shade is פסולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line of the משנה. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סוכה is supposed to give shade. If more sun comes in than shade is given, it is not a proper סוכה. The משנה does not say where the sunlight comes in from. The ברייתא will discuss that.

phrases.english: And [a sukkah] whose sunlight is greater than its shade is invalid
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to רבא's rulings about walls.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוכה with more sunlight than shade is פסולה.

steps.title: Only sunlight through the roof counts
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that the משנה means sunlight coming through the סכך, not sunlight coming through the walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'its sunlight' means sunlight that comes in because of the סכך, not because of the walls.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא explains what the משנה means by 'sunlight.' According to the תנא קמא, only the roof matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sunlight can come into a סוכה in two ways: through gaps in the סכך, or through gaps in the walls. The תנא קמא says only the first kind counts when you compare sun to shade. So a סוכה with thick סכך is כשרה even if a lot of sun comes in from the sides.
steps.confusionAlert: 'חמתה' means the sunlight coming in, not the heat. The question is about where that sunlight enters the סוכה.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
phrases.notes: Introduces a ברייתא.

phrases.english: 'Its sunlight' means sunlight because of the roofing,
and not because of the walls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the word חמתה in the משנה quoted in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only sunlight passing through the סכך is counted. Sunlight through the walls does not make the סוכה פסולה.

steps.title: רבי יאשיה: sunlight through the walls counts too
steps.stepSummary: רבי יאשיה disagrees. In his view, sunlight coming through the walls also counts toward making the סוכה פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יאשיה says: even sunlight that comes in because of the walls counts.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the second side of the מחלוקת. רבי יאשיה counts sunlight from the walls as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יאשיה, the walls must also mostly block the sun. If the walls have so many gaps that the sunlight is more than the shade, the סוכה is פסולה. This raises a question that the next step asks: why would walls need to give shade?

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who disagrees with the תנא קמא

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoshiya says:
Even [sunlight] because of the walls.
phrases.notes: This also makes the סוכה פסולה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sunlight through the walls also counts. If it makes the sunlight more than the shade, the סוכה is פסולה.

steps.title: What is רבי יאשיה's reason?
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר בר שלמיה, quoting אביי, asks for the source of רבי יאשיה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר בר שלמיה said in the name of אביי: What is רבי יאשיה's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יאשיה thinks the walls matter. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we think of shade as coming from the roof, so רבי יאשיה's view needs a source. The question is a real request for his reasoning, not an attack on him.

phrases.english: Rav Yeimar bar Shelemya said
in the name of Abaye:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yoshiya?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבי יאשיה's view from step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי יאשיה's view that the walls must also block sunlight.

steps.title: The פרוכת: a wall that the תורה calls covering
steps.stepSummary: The answer comes from a פסוק. The פרוכת was a wall, yet the תורה uses the word for covering (סכך). This shows that a wall must be like סכך, so it must also block the sun.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And you shall cover the ארון with the פרוכת.' The פרוכת was a wall, yet the תורה calls it covering. So we see that a wall must be like סכך.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers his own question with a פסוק about the פרוכת in the משכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פרוכת hung like a wall in front of the ארון. Still, the פסוק says 'וְסַכּוֹתָ,' from the same root as סכך. This teaches that a wall should do the job of סכך. Since סכך must give more shade than sun, the walls must too.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall cover; same root as סכך
The curtain that hung before the ארון in the משכן
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
So we see; it follows that

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא says only sunlight through the סכך counts. רבי יאשיה says sunlight through the walls counts too. His source is that the פרוכת, which was a wall, is called 'covering' in the פסוק.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows two different ideas of a סוכה wall. For the תנא קמא, a wall only has to enclose the space. For רבי יאשיה, a wall is part of the סוכה's shade, just like the סכך.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And you shall cover the Ark with the curtain,'
phrases.notes: שמות מ:ג

phrases.english: the curtain is a partition,
phrases.notes: It hung like a wall, not like a roof.

phrases.english: and yet the Merciful One calls it 'covering,'
so we see that we require a partition to be like the roofing.
phrases.notes: Like סכך, the wall must give more shade than sun.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק calls the פרוכת, which was a wall, by the word for covering. So a wall must be like סכך and must block more sun than it lets in.

steps.title: How do the רבנן read the פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the רבנן, who disagree with רבי יאשיה, explain the word וְסַכֹּתָ in the פסוק about the פרוכת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question. If the רבנן do not learn רבי יאשיה's rule from the פסוק, what do they do with the word וְסַכֹּתָ? This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה learned from וְסַכֹּתָ that a wall must be like סכך. The רבנן disagree with his rule. So the גמרא needs to know what they learn from the same word.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, here the ones who disagree with רבי יאשיה
"And you shall cover/screen", the word in the פסוק about the פרוכת

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? (How do they explain the verse?)
phrases.notes: A one-word question: what do the רבנן do with וְסַכֹּתָ?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the other side of the argument reads the פסוק that was just used as a proof for רבי יאשיה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the רבנן learn from the word וְסַכֹּתָ if they do not learn that walls must block the sun.

steps.title: The curtain was bent to look like a roof
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן learn from וְסַכֹּתָ that the top of the פרוכת was bent over a little, so it looked like a covering over the ארון.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word teaches that we bend the curtain a little at the top, so that it looks like a roof (סכך).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן read וְסַכֹּתָ as a description of how the פרוכת hung. Its top was bent over a bit so it looked like a covering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יאשיה, the word teaches a rule about walls: a wall must be like סכך. For the רבנן, the word only describes the shape of the curtain. So the פסוק has a meaning for them, and it teaches nothing about sunlight through walls.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יאשיה: וְסַכֹּתָ teaches that walls must be like סכך, so they must block the sun. רבנן: וְסַכֹּתָ only means the curtain was bent to look like a roof.

phrases.english: That word teaches that we bend it a little,
phrases.notes: The top of the פרוכת was folded over slightly.

phrases.english: so that it looks like a covering.
phrases.notes: The bent part looked like a roof over the ארון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 and closes the argument about walls.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן read וְסַכֹּתָ as describing the bent top of the פרוכת, not as a rule that walls must block sunlight.

steps.title: אביי lists eight תנאים who require a דירת קבע
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that רבי, רבי יאשיה, רבי יהודה, רבי שמעון, רבן גמליאל, בית שמאי, רבי אליעזר, and אחרים all hold that a סוכה must be a דירת קבע.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רבי, רבי יאשיה, רבי יהודה, רבי שמעון, רבן גמליאל, בית שמאי, רבי אליעזר, and אחרים all hold that we need a סוכה to be a permanent home.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts a new topic. He groups eight different תנאים under one shared idea: a סוכה must be a real, permanent-style home. The next steps will show where each one says this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these תנאים gave a different rule about סוכה. אביי says one principle lies behind all of them: the סוכה must be like a דירת קבע. This principle is the opposite of the view that a סוכה only needs to be a temporary home (דירת עראי).

keyTerms.meaning: They hold / are of the opinion
"Others", a name for a certain תנא (often said to be רבי מאיר)

steps.whyThisMatters: This list is a key tool for the whole מסכת. Many small rules about size, walls, and strength all come from one question: must a סוכה be permanent or temporary?
steps.confusionAlert: דירת קבע does not mean the סוכה must stand forever. It means it must be built well enough to be a real place to live, like a house, during the חג.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Rabbi (Yehuda HaNasi), and Rabbi Yoshiya, and Rabbi Yehuda,
and Rabbi Shimon, and Rabban Gamliel,
and Beit Shammai, and Rabbi Eliezer, and Acherim,
all of them hold:
we require a sukka to be a permanent dwelling.
phrases.notes: This is the shared principle.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: רַבִּי, וְרַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה, וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, וְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי, וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, וַאֲחֵרִים — כּוּלְּהוּ סְבִירָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the specific argument and groups רבי יאשיה, together with seven other תנאים, under one principle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eight תנאים share the view that a סוכה must be a דירת קבע.

steps.title: רבי's source: a סוכה must be four by four אמות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי holds דירת קבע, from a ברייתא where he says a סוכה smaller than 4x4 אמות is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי: as a ברייתא teaches, רבי says any סוכה that is not four אמות by four אמות is פסולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins going through אביי's list one name at a time. First it shows where רבי says a סוכה must be a permanent home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Four אמות by four אמות is the smallest size of a real living space. רבי requires a סוכה to be at least this big. That shows he sees a סוכה as a permanent home.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
Four אמות by four אמות, the minimum size of a living space

phrases.english: Rabbi: as it is taught in a baraita,
phrases.notes: The first name on אביי's list.

phrases.english: Rabbi says:
any sukka that does not have
four cubits by four cubits,
is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the first name in אביי's list.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי holds a סוכה must be a דירת קבע.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא where רבי requires at least 4x4 אמות.

steps.title: רבי יאשיה's source: what we already said
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points back to רבי יאשיה's rule that the walls must block sunlight, like a real house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יאשיה: that which we already said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second name on the list. It does not bring a new source. It points back to what we just learned about רבי יאשיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה said that sunlight through the walls also makes the סוכה פסולה. Walls that let in sun are not like a real house's walls. So requiring solid walls shows he sees the סוכה as a permanent home.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoshiya:
that which we stated.
phrases.notes: Refers back to steps 8–10: the walls must also block the sun.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues through אביי's list with the second name.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יאשיה holds a סוכה must be a דירת קבע.
steps.raayaSupportSource: His earlier view that sunlight through the walls makes the סוכה פסולה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה allows a סוכה taller than twenty אמות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that רבי יהודה holds דירת קבע from the משנה where he allows a סוכה higher than twenty אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה holds this too, as we learned in a משנה: a סוכה that is taller than twenty אמות is פסולה, but רבי יהודה says it is כשרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is giving the next proof for אביי's list. It shows that רבי יהודה holds a סוכה should be a דירת קבע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A very tall סוכה (over twenty אמות) needs strong, permanent walls to stand up. Since רבי יהודה still says it is כשרה, he must not require a temporary hut. So he holds a סוכה can be, and should be, like a real house.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Twenty אמות (cubits), the height limit of the רבנן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not get confused: here רבי יהודה is the one who says the tall סוכה is כשרה. That is exactly the proof. Allowing a סוכה that must be built strong and permanent shows that he holds דירת קבע.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda, as we learned in a Mishnah:
A sukkah that is tall
more than twenty cubits is invalid;
Rabbi Yehuda says it is valid.
phrases.notes: Above twenty אמות, one must build a sturdy, permanent structure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of proofs for אביי's statement, moving from רבי יאשיה to רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה holds a סוכה must be a דירת קבע.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה at the start of מסכת סוכה: a סוכה higher than twenty אמות is פסולה, and רבי יהודה says it is כשרה.

steps.title: רבי שמעון requires three full walls plus a fourth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that רבי שמעון holds דירת קבע from a ברייתא where he requires three proper walls and a fourth wall of at least a טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון holds this too, as a ברייתא teaches: a סוכה needs two proper walls and a third wall of even one טפח. רבי שמעון says: it needs three proper walls and a fourth wall of even one טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the proof for רבי שמעון. He requires more walls than the רבנן do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן are fine with a סוכה that is open on more of its sides. רבי שמעון wants walls on all four sides, even if the fourth is tiny. That makes the סוכה closed in like a real house, so he holds דירת קבע.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon, as it is taught in a baraita:
Two walls in the standard way,
and a third, even one handbreadth;
Rabbi Shimon says: three walls in the standard way,
and a fourth, even one handbreadth.
phrases.notes: Walls on all four sides, like a real house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next name in אביי's list after רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון holds a סוכה must be a דירת קבע.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי שמעון requires three proper walls and a fourth wall of a טפח.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל rejects a סוכה on a wagon or boat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that רבן גמליאל holds דירת קבע from a ברייתא where he says a סוכה on a wagon or boat is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל holds this too, as a ברייתא teaches: if someone builds his סוכה on top of a wagon or on top of a boat, רבן גמליאל says it is פסולה, and רבי עקיבא says it is כשרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the proof for רבן גמליאל. He does not accept a סוכה that moves around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A house stays in one place. A סוכה on a wagon or a boat keeps moving, so it is not like a real home. Since רבן גמליאל says it is פסולה, he holds a סוכה must be a דירת קבע.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel, as it is taught in a baraita:
One who makes his sukkah on top of a wagon
or on top of a boat,
Rabban Gamliel says it is invalid,
phrases.notes: A moving structure is not a permanent home.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Akiva says it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next name in אביי's list after רבי שמעון.
steps.raayaObject: That רבן גמליאל holds a סוכה must be a דירת קבע.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבן גמליאל says a סוכה on a wagon or boat is פסולה, against רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: בית שמאי require room for a person and his table
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that בית שמאי hold דירת קבע from a משנה where they say a סוכה is פסולה if it only fits a person's head and most of his body while his table is in the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי hold this too, as we learned in a משנה: if a person's head and most of his body were in the סוכה and his table was inside the house, בית שמאי say it is פסולה, and בית הלל say it is כשרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the proof for בית שמאי. They want the סוכה big enough to hold the person together with his table.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real home has room for you and your table. A tiny סוכה that only fits your head and most of your body, with the table left in the house, is not like a real home. Since בית שמאי say it is פסולה, they hold a סוכה must be a דירת קבע.

keyTerms.meaning: His head and most of his body

steps.whatToRemember: All the proofs share one idea. Each of these תנאים wants the סוכה to work like a real house: tall and sturdy is fine (רבי יהודה), closed on all sides (רבי שמעון), standing in one place (רבן גמליאל), and big enough to live and eat in (בית שמאי).
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the support for most of אביי's list. It shows that the idea of סוכה as a דירת קבע runs through many different מחלוקות in the מסכת.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai, as we learned in a Mishnah:
One whose head and most of his body were in the sukkah
and his table was inside the house,
Beit Shammai say it is invalid,
phrases.notes: Too small to be a real dwelling.

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next name in אביי's list after רבן גמליאל.
steps.raayaObject: That בית שמאי hold a סוכה must be a דירת קבע.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה where בית שמאי say a סוכה is פסולה when it holds only a person's head and most of his body, with his table in the house.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר requires a real house: a סוכה needs a roof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that רבי אליעזר holds דירת קבע from a משנה. There he says a tent-shaped סוכה, or one leaned against a wall, is פסולה because it has no roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר also holds that a סוכה must be like a permanent home, as we learned in a משנה: If someone makes his סוכה like a pointed hut, or leans it against a wall, רבי אליעזר says it is פסולה because it has no roof. The חכמים say it is כשרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds רבי אליעזר to its list of תנאים who say a סוכה must be like a real house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pointed, A-frame hut has walls that slope until they meet at the top, so there is no flat roof. A real house has a roof, so רבי אליעזר's reason, 'it has no roof,' shows he measures a סוכה by the standard of a permanent home.

keyTerms.meaning: A pointed, tent-like hut whose walls slope up and meet at the top
He leaned it against a wall (branches slanting from the ground to the wall)

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer — as we learned in a Mishnah:
phrases.notes: This continues the list of תנאים who hold a סוכה must be a דירת קבע.

phrases.english: One who makes his sukkah like a kind of pointed hut,
or who leaned it against a wall,
Rabbi Eliezer declares it invalid
because it has no roof,
and the Sages declare it valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another item in the same list of proofs that various תנאים hold דירת קבע.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר holds a סוכה must be a דירת קבע.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a צריף-shaped סוכה, which רבי אליעזר disqualifies because it has no roof.

steps.title: אחרים require a real house: a סוכה needs corners
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that אחרים hold דירת קבע from a ברייתא. There they say a round סוכה shaped like a dovecote is פסולה because it has no corners.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחרים also hold this, as a ברייתא teaches: אחרים say a סוכה built like a dovecote is פסולה, because it has no corners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the last name on its list. אחרים also require a סוכה to look like a real house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dovecote (pigeon coop) was round. A normal house has corners, so disqualifying a cornerless סוכה shows that אחרים use a permanent home as the model for a סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others': an unnamed תנא or group of תנאים cited in ברייתות
As it was taught in a ברייתא
A dovecote, a round pigeon coop

steps.whatToRemember: The full list of תנאים who hold a סוכה must be a דירת קבע: רבי (at least four אמות by four אמות), רבי יאשיה (walls that block sunlight), רבי יהודה (a סוכה higher than twenty אמות is allowed), רבי שמעון (three proper walls plus a fourth of a טפח), רבן גמליאל (no סוכה on a wagon or boat), בית שמאי (it must hold one's head, body, and table), רבי אליעזר (it needs a roof), and אחרים (it needs corners).

phrases.english: Acherim — as it was taught in a Baraita,
Acherim say:
A sukkah made like a dovecote is invalid,
because it has no corners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final proof in the same list, which closes the דירת קבע section.
steps.raayaObject: That אחרים hold a סוכה must be a דירת קבע.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which אחרים disqualify a round, dovecote-shaped סוכה because it has no corners.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a round furnace-shaped סוכה needs room for 24 people around its edge
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that a round, furnace-shaped סוכה is כשרה only if its edge has room for twenty-four people to sit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: A סוכה shaped like a furnace (round) is כשרה if its edge has enough room for twenty-four people to sit. If not, it is פסולה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי יוחנן gives a rule for how big a completely round סוכה must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike אחרים, רבי יוחנן does not disqualify a round סוכה just because it has no corners. He only demands that it be large enough, measured by how many people can sit along its edge. A large measurement like this suggests he holds a strict minimum size, which leads to the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: A furnace or kiln, which is round in shape

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יוחנן agrees with אחרים that a round סוכה is always פסולה. He says a round סוכה can be כשרה if it is big enough. The גמרא next asks whose view this follows, and then challenges the number twenty-four with a calculation. The explanation of the number comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
A sukkah made like a furnace (round),
if there is around its edge
enough room to sit in it
twenty-four people, it is valid,
and if not, it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: סוּכָּה הָעֲשׂוּיָה כְּכִבְשָׁן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. It follows naturally from the discussion of round סוכות (the dovecote case) but brings in a new ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A round סוכה is כשרה only if its circumference has room for twenty-four people to sit.

steps.title: Whose view is רבי יוחנן following?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא's opinion רבי יוחנן's ruling is based on.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom did רבי יוחנן rule this way?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which earlier opinion matches רבי יוחנן's large size requirement. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Room for twenty-four people is a big measurement. The גמרא wants to know which תנא demands a סוכה this large, since not everyone does.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? (Whose opinion is this?)

phrases.english: According to whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's minimum-size opinion lies behind רבי יוחנן's requirement of room for twenty-four people.

steps.title: It follows רבי, who requires four by four אמות
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's ruling follows רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא), who says any סוכה smaller than four אמות by four אמות is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows רבי, who said: Any סוכה that does not measure four אמות by four אמות is פסולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן follows רבי, who requires the largest minimum size for a סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most opinions accept a smaller minimum size, so only רבי's large four-by-four requirement could explain a measurement as big as twenty-four people. Exactly how twenty-four seats around the edge matches רבי's four-by-four minimum is not yet explained. The גמרא questions the number in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'רבי': רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה
Four cubits by four cubits, רבי's minimum area for a סוכה

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties רבי יוחנן's round-סוכה rule to a specific minimum-size opinion. That link sets up the גמרא's coming calculation of how a four-by-four square fits inside a circle.

phrases.english: According to Rebbi, who said:
Any sukkah that does not have

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת עַל אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.english: four cubits by four cubits is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן follows רבי, who requires a minimum of four אמות by four אמות.

steps.title: The math suggests twelve people should be enough, not twenty-four
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's number. A person sitting takes up one אמה, and a circle's circumference is three times its width. A round סוכה with room for twelve people already has a twelve-אמה edge and is four אמות across. So why does he require twenty-four?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, since a person sitting takes up one אמה, and any circle that measures three טפחים around is one טפח wide, twelve people should be enough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is checking רבי יוחנן's number with simple math. The math seems to show that he asked for double what is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that רבי יוחנן follows רבי, who requires a סוכה four אמות wide. Each sitting person takes one אמה of the edge, so twenty-four people means an edge of twenty-four אמות. But a circle is one-third as wide as it measures around. So an edge of only twelve אמות (twelve people) already gives a width of four אמות. The question is why רבי יוחנן doubled the number.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, since — introduces a logical calculation that leads to a challenge
A person sits in one אמה — each sitting person takes up one cubit of space
Circumference, the distance around a circle
Width; here, the diameter straight across the circle
Handbreadth, a unit of measurement (six טפחים make one אמה)

steps.confusionAlert: The 3-to-1 rule is stated in טפחים, but it is a ratio, so it works the same way for אמות. Also, '24' and '12' here are numbers of people. Since each person takes one אמה, they are also the circumference in אמות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge forces the גמרא to explain exactly what shape must fit inside the round סוכה. That explanation shows how round and square measurements relate in הלכה.

phrases.english: Now, since
phrases.notes: Signals that a calculation is coming, and it will lead to a question.

phrases.english: a person sits in one cubit,
phrases.notes: So 24 people around the edge means an edge of 24 אמות.

phrases.english: anything whose circumference is three handbreadths
phrases.notes: The standard Talmudic ratio for a circle: 3 around for every 1 across.

phrases.english: has a width of one handbreadth,
phrases.notes: The width straight across (the diameter) is one-third of the circumference.

phrases.english: twelve should suffice!
phrases.notes: A 12-אמה circumference gives a width of 4 אמות, which is רבי's minimum. So why 24?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that רבי יוחנן follows רבי's four-by-four-אמות minimum (Step 24). It then argues that this minimum would require only twelve people around a round סוכה, not twenty-four.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's requirement (Step 22) that a round סוכה must seat twenty-four people around its edge
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One person takes one אמה, and a circle's width is one-third of its circumference. So 12 people means a 12-אמה circumference, which gives a 4-אמה width. That already meets רבי's minimum, so 24 seems to be double what is needed.
